aker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Across the following verses, transitions between argument, threat, excuse, and warning unify varied subjects through elevated composition.","anchor":"ثم اتل ما بعدها من الآي واعرف وجه الخلوص من شيء إلى شيء","mentions":["40:4"]},{"verses":["40:5","40:6"],"words":["ليأخذوه"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The phrase “to seize him” is uniquely forceful; replacing it with “kill,” “stone,” “banish,” or similar verbs would lose the passage’s originality and grandeur.","anchor":"وهل يسد مسده في الأصالة نكتة ولو وضع موضع ذلك ليقتلوه","mentions":[]},{"verses":["40:5","40:6"],"words":["*"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The cited passage has four sections in its first verse and two in the next, whose arrangement contributes to its distinction.","anchor":"الآية الأولى أربعة فصول والثانية فصلان","mentions":[]}]}' in /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/v7/work/t1_s096_20261009/out/luna-max/c1313.jsonl
2026-10-09T06:00:25.336961Z ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=apply_patch verification failed: Failed to find context '{"loc":"BAQILLANI:v1p175","rows":[{"verses":["3:37"],"words":["*"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"Other poets’ comparisons of the Pleiades equal or surpass the celebrated example, showing that this kind of poetic invention is common rather than unique.","anchor":"وفي جملة ما نقلناه ما يزيد على تشبيهه في الحسن أو يساويه أو يقاربه","mentions":[]},{"verses":["3:37"],"words":["*"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The word “appeared” is unnecessary in the Pleiades simile: the comparison works whether the constellation is high, rising, or setting.","anchor":"فقوله تعرضت من الكلام الذي يستغني عنه لأنه يشبه أثناء الوشاح بالثريا","mentions":[]},{"verses":["3:37"],"words":["*"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The sash image is confused: the poet treats the Pleiades as one piece of a sash, then describes its plural middle sections; he meant a single piece.","anchor":"وفيه أن الثريا كقطعة من الوشاح المفصل فلا معنى تعرض لقوله أثناء الوشاح","mentions":[]},{"verses":["3:37"],"words":["*"],"type":"rhetoric","speaker":"author","stance":"holds","claim":"The poem’s sequence is poorly ordered: it mentions the encounter’s pleasure, timing, and guards before describing the woman’s state at his arrival; “by the curtain” is filler.","anchor":"انظر إلى البيت الثاني الأول والأبيات التي قبله كيف خلط في النظم وفرط في التأليف","mentions":[]},{"verses":["3:37"],"words":["*"],"type":"reports","speaker":"الأصمعي","stance":"reports","claim":"Al-Aṣmaʿī explains “what recourse do you have?” to mean that the lover has no way to approach while people are around her.","anchor":"وأما البيت الثاني ففيه تعليق واختلال ذكر الأصمعي أن معنى قوله ما لك حيلة","mentions":[]}]}' in /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/v7/work/t1_s096_20261009/out/luna-max/c1313.jsonl
